title: Cap. X Arg. X Major/Minor: non-elect = those to whom God never destined efficacious means; many such exist; therefore many are passed by before foresight of final unbelief
pass_a_gloss: As concerns everlasting life, he is considered passed by, non-elect, or reprobate antecedently unto his foreseen unbelief, unto whom God from eternity has not destined, prepared, and unto whom in time he has not given efficacious means unto begetting faith and perseverance, and infallibly obtaining everlasting life: But unto many (as the event itself declares) God has neither destined, nor prepared, nor given this efficacious grace. Therefore many are passed by or non-elect antecedently unto their foreseen unbelief and final contumacy in the same. Concerning the Minor there can be no question: let us therefore unfold and confirm the Major.
pass_b_english: As for everlasting life: the one passed by, non-elect, or reprobate before foresight of his unbelief is the one to whom God from eternity neither destined nor prepared, and in time did not give, efficacious means to beget faith and perseverance and obtain everlasting life infallibly. But to many—as the event itself shows—God neither destined nor prepared nor gave that efficacious grace. Therefore many are passed by or non-elect before foresight of their unbelief and final stubbornness in it. The Minor is beyond dispute; so let us open and confirm the Major.
source_text: Quod attinet ad vitam aeternam, ille antecedenter ad praevisam suam infidelitatem praeteritus, non-electus, sive reprobatus consideratur, cui Deus ab aeterno non destinavit, praeparavit, ac cui in tempore non donavit efficacia media ad fidem et perseverantiam ingenerandam, vitamque aeternam infallibiliter obtinendam: At multis (sicut eventus ipse declarat) Deus nec destinavit, nec praeparavit, nec donavit hanc gratiam efficacem. Ergo, multi sunt praeteriti sive non-electi antecedenter ad praevisam suam infidelitatem et contumaciam finalem in eadem. De Minore nulla potest esse quaestio: Majorem igitur explicemus et confirmemus.
